findings.message: Editing a private source URL loses its stored token. The UI sends "*" under the new URL, but this lookup only checks existingCred.Env[newURL], while the token remains keyed by the old URL. The old key is then dropped. Changing a branch or adding a .git suffix therefore silently removes authentication. Preserve the association explicitly when renaming a source.

URL normalization does not normalize the corresponding SourceURLCredentials key. Entering gitlab.com/org/private.git with a PAT produces an HTTPS source URL, but the token remains keyed by the scheme-less input and is discarded by the activeURLs check. The request succeeds without storing the token, so the private source cannot sync.

Hardcoding the GitHub authentication username prevents private repositories on other HTTPS hosts from working. For example, [Bitbucket Cloud requires x-token-auth for repository access tokens](https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/using-access-tokens/). Supplying that username in the source URL cannot help because parseGitURL discards URL user information. Support a configurable username or the appropriate authentication scheme for each host.

Classifying every gitlab.com URL as a repository breaks previously supported raw-file sources such as https://gitlab.com/org/repo/-/raw/main/catalog.yaml. These previously used the HTTP/YAML path; now the parser interprets -/raw/main/catalog.yaml as a branch and rejects it. Keep GitLab raw-file URLs on the raw catalog path.

The two-component path requirement rejects valid repositories hosted directly beneath an HTTPS host, such as https://git.example.com/catalog.git. isGitRepoURL recognizes this URL, but parsing fails before reaching the .git boundary logic. Generic git hosts do not necessarily have an organization component; allow a single repository path component when the .git boundary is present.
